extracted.intended_audience: anyone interested in fact-checking and internet research (citizen fact-checkers, journalists, concerned readers)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance and component skills for performing fact-checking and internet research: spotting misleading content, verifying images and claims, using archives and experts, and understanding cognitive/social pitfalls that enable misinformation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nose for bunk
rubrics_metrics.description: A healthy skepticism or instinct to suspect false or misleading claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate an instinct to question dubious content rather than accept it at face value; use that suspicion as the starting point for investigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment to answering misinformation with hard facts and evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Use verifiable facts and evidence to rebut or evaluate misinformation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize primary sources, documentation, and corroborated data when assessing claims; avoid speculation and clearly separate verified facts from hypotheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination to dig until you get to the truth
rubrics_metrics.description: Persistence in research—keep digging through sources until the claim is resolved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow leads, cross-check multiple sources, and keep investigating (archives, experts, network connections) rather than stopping at the first plausible explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Connecting the dots between questionable social media accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: Map and link related accounts or posts to understand origin, amplification, or coordination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for patterns, shared content, timing, and account metadata to identify networks, originators, or coordinated campaigns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reverse-image search on suspect photographs
rubrics_metrics.description: Use reverse-image search tools to find original sources, prior uses, or manipulated versions of an image.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Run images through Google Images, TinEye, and other reverse-search tools; check dates and contexts of prior matches to detect repurposing or misattribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contacting expert sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Reach out to subject-matter experts to verify technical or specialized claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify credible experts, ask specific questions, and document expert responses; use expert input to interpret technical evidence or correct misunderstandings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deep dive into online newspaper archives
rubrics_metrics.description: Search historical news archives to verify timelines, prior reporting, or provenance of claims/images.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use newspaper archives and library databases to find contemporaneous reporting and original context; preserve citations and screenshots where needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understanding logical fallacies
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize common faulty arguments and reasoning patterns that underpin misinformation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Learn fallacy names and examples so you can identify when claims rely on poor logic rather than evidence; use this to explain why a claim is misleading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Archiving on the Internet (preserving records)
rubrics_metrics.description: Create and consult archived snapshots of web content to preserve evidence and track changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use archive.org, perma.cc, or other archiving tools to capture and reference content; archived records are essential to show how content appeared at a given time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognizing the Black Sheep Effect (social-bias insight)
rubrics_metrics.description: Be aware of social-psychological biases (e.g., harsher judgment of deviants within one's own group) that affect interpretation of social media content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply awareness of biases to avoid misattributing motives or judging sources unfairly; consider group dynamics when assessing claims and reactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identifying sponsored content / native advertising
rubrics_metrics.description: Detect content designed to look like editorial material but paid for by advertisers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for disclosures, unusual formatting, or content that serves a promotional aim; verify claims in such pieces against independent reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awareness of confirmation bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize the tendency to accept information that confirms preexisting beliefs and discount opposing evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actively seek disconfirming evidence and alternative explanations; document why a conclusion was reached and what contrary data was considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detecting echo chambers
rubrics_metrics.description: Understand environments where information is amplified within like-minded groups and opposing views are excluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine networks, sources, and shared content to see if a claim circulates mainly within an insular community; broaden searches to reach beyond that bubble.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spotting deepfakes
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify synthetic or manipulated audio/video that falsely depicts events or people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for visual artifacts, inconsistent lighting/eye movement, audio glitches; corroborate with independent footage, metadata, and expert analysis when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seeing through disingenuous captions (clearing the frame)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether captions misrepresent the visual content by omitting context or altering meaning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare images/videos with their original sources and surrounding reporting to detect caption-driven framing; verify who made the claim and the original caption context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performing reverse image searches (how-to details)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use specific techniques to search by image and interpret results effectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Try multiple reverse-image services, crop or search by variants, check timestamps and pages where image appears, and look for the earliest instance to establish provenance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluating whether research is peer-reviewed
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the credibility of scientific claims by checking if underlying research has undergone peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look up the journal, submission and review process, and whether the work is a preprint; prefer peer-reviewed, replicated studies for factual claims about science.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spotting fabricated messages on clothing (media-literacy detail)
rubrics_metrics.description: Detect when images of clothing (e.g., T-shirts) have had text or messages fabricated or misattributed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inspect high-resolution images, seek original photos, and verify claims about slogans by checking manufacturer or event sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring virtue signaling on social media
rubrics_metrics.description: Be alert to performative displays that may mislead about sincerity or the prevalence of a viewpoint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish between widespread grassroots activity and isolated virtue-signaling posts; check for organized campaigns or astroturfing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detecting and avoiding online scams
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify typical scam tactics (e.g., 'exclusive reward', fake coupons) and evaluate whether offers are legitimate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for red flags like pressure, requests for payment/personal data, and poor grammar; verify via official channels before engaging or sharing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identifying ad arbitrage clickbait
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize sites that split content or use misleading headlines to generate ad revenue rather than inform.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note multi-page articles, sensationalist phrasing, and lack of substantive reporting; avoid citing such sources as authoritative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honing search skills
rubrics_metrics.description: Use advanced search techniques and operators to find relevant, authoritative information efficiently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Learn boolean operators, site: searches, date filtering, and other engine features to zero in on primary sources and earliest reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identifying red flags in suspicious rumors
rubrics_metrics.description: Spot common techniques and signals that indicate a rumor is dubious or manufactured.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Watch for anonymous sourcing, lack of evidence, circular sourcing (copypasta), emotionally charged language, and rapid, unverified spread.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identifying the 'right' results in a search engine
rubrics_metrics.description: Discern which search results are credible and relevant rather than just popular or optimized for clicks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer primary sources, reputable outlets, and documents over listicles or SEO-optimized pages; check result dates and original reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spotting coordinated inauthentic behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Detect groups of accounts acting in coordination to mislead, amplify, or manipulate discourse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for synchronized posting, reused images/text, similar account creation patterns, and accounts pushing the same narratives across platforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spotting social media bots
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify automated accounts used to amplify content or distort engagement metrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine posting frequency, timing, profile completeness, and content patterns; use bot-detection tools and network analysis to corroborate suspicions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguishing misinformation vs. disinformation
rubrics_metrics.description: Understand the difference between false information shared without malicious intent (misinformation) and deliberately deceptive content (disinformation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider sender intent and evidence of coordination or fabrication when classifying a claim; this affects how you respond and report it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognizing copypasta (recycled text)
rubrics_metrics.description: Detect when identical or near-identical text is being copied and spread across platforms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search verbatim phrases to find origins; copypasta can indicate mass-sharing of an unverified claim rather than independent corroboration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fact-checking racial propaganda
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply specific scrutiny to racist or propaganda content to identify manipulation, falsehoods, or decontextualization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify sources, check historical context, consult experts in race/history when needed, and be mindful of how imagery and rhetoric are used to inflame.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identifying troll bait
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize content designed to provoke outrage or emotional reactions rather than convey accurate information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid amplifying inflammatory posts; check claims before reacting and examine motives and origin of provocative content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understanding 'shadow-ban' claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Know what shadow-banning refers to and how platform moderation, algorithmic demotion, or visibility changes differ from coordinated suppression claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate platform policies and observable metadata rather than relying on anecdotal reports of 'shadow-ban.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Understanding the Mandela Effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Be aware of collective memory errors where groups misremember facts or events, which can fuel false claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use archival records and contemporaneous documentation to test remembered facts against verifiable evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognizing playful/linguistic phenomena (e.g., Spoonerism) that can confuse readers
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish linguistic slips and jokes from factual claims to avoid misinterpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check intent and original context before treating unusual phrasing as evidence of a factual claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understanding a 'misinformation ouroboros' (self-reinforcing cycles)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize how misinformation can feed on itself and be recycled in loops that appear to corroborate the falsehood.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trace sources back to the earliest origin rather than taking multiple downstream reposts as independent verification.
